servers.name: Amortization
servers.tagline: Loan and lease schedules from the agreement, exact to the cent.
servers.plain: Give it the terms of a loan or lease and it returns the payment, the interest and every period of the schedule. It keeps a register of your agreements, prices an early repayment and writes the monthly journal your bookkeeper needs.

cases.title: Check a bank's loan quote
cases.persona: Owner of a bakery in Krakow

steps.does: Builds the 60-period schedule without storing anything

cases.result: A payment of EUR 483.32 a month and about EUR 3,999 of interest over five years, with the balance for every month.
cases.minutes_basis: INFERRED: building an amortization table in a spreadsheet takes 20-30 min

cases.title: Price an early payoff

steps.does: Finds the stored van loan
Recomputes the schedule with the extra GBP 5,000

cases.result: The new end date, the periods saved and the interest saved, next to the old schedule. Pro feature.
cases.minutes_basis: INFERRED: re-running a schedule by hand with an extra payment takes 30+ min

cases.title: Book the month's loan entries
cases.persona: Freelance bookkeeper in Dublin with 4 client loans
cases.prompt: Give me the October journal for every loan: interest expense, principal and the cash out.

steps.does: Splits each October payment into interest and principal
Totals the balance outstanding per currency

cases.result: Ready-to-post debit and credit lines per loan, plus the total debt still owed. Pro feature.
cases.minutes_basis: INFERRED: splitting 4 loan payments from bank statements takes 20-30 min

top_tools.plain: Payment, interest and balance for every period. Free and unlimited

faq.q: Is the schedule itself free?
faq.a: Yes. loan_schedule is free and unlimited on every tier. The free tier caps the stored register at 3 loans.

faq.q: Does it round like my bank?
faq.a: It works in integer minor units, so every amount is exact to the cent. Your bank may round the last payment differently. The schedule shows each period so you can compare.

servers.name: Asset Register

Net book value by category with the year's charge

faq.a: No. It computes schedules and journals. Filing stays with you or your accountant.

faq.a: No. It checks pages you name. It doesn't discover links you don't know about.

faq.a: No. No store is opened and no file is written. Every check fetches the page again.

faq.q: Will a banking app read the payment QR?
faq.a: The SEPA QR follows the EPC format that many EU banking apps scan. Test one with your own bank app before you print a batch.

faq.q: Is SVG good enough to print?
faq.a: Yes. SVG has no fixed resolution, so it prints sharp at any size. PNG is the Pro option.

cases.prompt: Add to project Atlas: fix login bug (high, 90 min, due Wednesday), write API docs (3 hours, due Friday).

steps.does: Adds both tasks with estimates and due dates
Shows the board

cases.result: The Atlas board with both tasks, their estimates and due dates.
cases.minutes_basis: INFERRED: opening a project tool and adding tasks takes 5 min

cases.title: What is overdue
cases.prompt: What's overdue across all my projects?

steps.does: Lists overdue tasks across boards

cases.result: Each late task with project, due date and priority.
cases.minutes_basis: INFERRED: checking three boards takes 5 min

cases.title: Friday review
cases.prompt: Log 2 hours on the API docs, mark it done, and give me the weekly review.

steps.does: Adds 120 minutes
Moves it to done
Done, slipped and estimate vs actual

cases.result: A review of the week with estimate against actual time per task.
cases.minutes_basis: INFERRED: writing a weekly status note takes 15 min

top_tools.name: task_add
top_tools.plain: Adds a task with due date and estimate

top_tools.name: weekly_review
top_tools.plain: Done, slipped and estimate vs actual

free: Weekly review for the current week
pro: Weekly review for any past week

faq.q: Does it sync with Trello or Jira?
faq.a: No. It's a standalone board. On the local install it lives in a file on your machine.

faq.q: Can it start a timer?
faq.a: task_start_timer returns the arguments for the time tracker's timer and records the link. It doesn't start a timer on its own.

servers.name: Leave
servers.tagline: Leave requests, approvals and balances for a small team.
servers.plain: Add your staff with their annual allowance. Log requests for vacation, sick, unpaid or parental leave, approve or reject them, and see each balance. Ask who is out in any date range before you agree to a deadline.

cases.title: Approve a holiday
cases.persona: Owner of a 6-person agency in Krakow
cases.prompt: Ania asks for 5 days of vacation from 22 to 26 December. Approve it and show her balance.

steps.does: Logs the vacation request
Approves it
Shows days remaining

cases.result: Approved, and her balance shows the 5 days taken from her 26-day allowance.
cases.minutes_basis: INFERRED: updating a leave spreadsheet and replying takes 10 min

cases.title: Who is out for the launch
cases.persona: Office manager at a Dublin software firm
cases.prompt: Who is out between 1 and 14 December?

steps.does: Lists everyone out, day by day

cases.result: Each person out in the range, pending requests shown as planned.
cases.minutes_basis: INFERRED: cross-checking a shared calendar takes 10 min

steps.does: Imports the requests in bulk
Writes a calendar file

cases.minutes_basis: INFERRED: entering 25 people's requests by hand takes an hour or more

faq.q: Which leave types are supported?
faq.a: Vacation, sick, unpaid and parental.

faq.q: Does it know my country's legal allowance?
faq.a: No. You set each employee's annual allowance and carried-over days.
